text: This Handbook sets out the academic rules that apply to all undergraduate students of Nakawa University for the 2025/2026 academic year. Where this Handbook conflicts with a Programme Handbook, this Handbook prevails on matters of general academic regulation. Where it conflicts with the Examination Regulations on matters of assessment conduct, the Examination Regulations prevail. All students are deemed to have read this Handbook upon registration. Ignorance of a rule contained in this Handbook is not accepted as grounds for appeal.
doc_title: Nakawa University Academic Handbook 2025/2026
citation: Nakawa University Academic Handbook 2025/2026, s. 1 (Purpose and Scope), p. 1

text: Every student must register at the beginning of each semester. Registration consists of three steps which must all be completed: Payment of at least sixty per cent (60%) of the semester tuition. Online course selection through the Student Portal. Biometric confirmation at the Faculty Registrar's office. A student who has not completed all three steps by the close of the registration period is not a registered student for that semester. Unregistered students may not attend classes, access the Learning Management System, or sit any assessment. The registration period opens on the first day of the semester and closes at the end of the third week of teaching. Late registration is permitted during the fourth week only, on payment of a late registration fee of UGX 50,000.
doc_title: Nakawa University Academic Handbook 2025/2026
citation: Nakawa University Academic Handbook 2025/2026, s. 2 (Registration), p. 1

text: A registered student may add or drop courses during the add/drop period, subject to the limits in this section. The add/drop period for Semester I of 2025/2026 closes on Friday 26 September 2025 at 17:00 East Africa Time. The add/drop period for Semester II closes on Friday 13 February 2026 at 17:00 East Africa Time. Adding or dropping is performed by the student on the Student Portal and must then be approved by the Head of Department. A change that is not approved by the Head of Department before the deadline is void, and the student remains registered for the original course set. The following limits apply during add/drop: A student may not exceed the maximum semester load of 24 credit units, nor fall below the minimum full-time load of 15 credit units.
doc_title: Nakawa University Academic Handbook 2025/2026
citation: Nakawa University Academic Handbook 2025/2026, s. 3 (Course Add and Drop), p. 2

text: The following limits apply during add/drop: A student may not exceed the maximum semester load of 24 credit units, nor fall below the minimum full-time load of 15 credit units. A student may not add a course whose teaching has already exceeded three sessions. A student may not drop a core course required by their programme. Only elective courses may be dropped. A course dropped within the add/drop period does not appear on the academic transcript and attracts no financial penalty. After the add/drop deadline the student is academically and financially committed to the registered course set. A course abandoned after the deadline is graded as F (Fail) and counts in the cumulative grade point average.
doc_title: Nakawa University Academic Handbook 2025/2026
citation: Nakawa University Academic Handbook 2025/2026, s. 3 (Course Add and Drop), p. 2

text: Withdrawal is distinct from dropping. Withdrawal applies after the add/drop deadline has passed and requires documented grounds. A student may apply to withdraw from a course up to the end of the ninth week of teaching. The application is made on Form AR/7, is supported by documentary evidence, and is decided by the Faculty Board. Acceptable grounds are limited to: Documented illness or injury, supported by a report from University Health Services or a recognised medical practitioner. Bereavement of an immediate family member.
doc_title: Nakawa University Academic Handbook 2025/2026
citation: Nakawa University Academic Handbook 2025/2026, s. 4 (Withdrawal from a Course), p. 3

text: Documented illness or injury, supported by a report from University Health Services or a recognised medical practitioner. Bereavement of an immediate family member. A documented timetable clash created by an administrative error of the University. A course from which a student has withdrawn with approval is recorded on the transcript with the code W. A grade of W carries no grade points and does not affect the cumulative grade point average, but the credit units still count toward the maximum permitted programme duration. An application to withdraw after the ninth week is not considered except under the Exceptional Circumstances procedure in Section 9.
doc_title: Nakawa University Academic Handbook 2025/2026
citation: Nakawa University Academic Handbook 2025/2026, s. 4 (Withdrawal from a Course), p. 3

text: A student must attend at least seventy-five per cent (75%) of the scheduled sessions of a course to be eligible to sit the final examination for that course. Attendance is recorded by the course lecturer and published on the Student Portal by the end of the eleventh week. A student whose attendance falls below 75% is issued a Missing Attendance Notice and has five working days to submit an explanation to the Head of Department. Where the explanation is not accepted, the student is barred from the final examination and is graded F for that course.
doc_title: Nakawa University Academic Handbook 2025/2026
citation: Nakawa University Academic Handbook 2025/2026, s. 5 (Attendance), p. 3

text: Nakawa University uses a five-point grading scheme. Marks are reported as whole numbers out of 100. | Mark range | Letter grade | Grade point | Interpretation | |---|---|---|---| | 80 - 100 | A | 5.0 | Excellent | | 70 - 79 | B | 4.0 | Very good | | 60 - 69 | C | 3.0 | Good | | 50 - 59 | D | 2.0 | Pass | | 0 - 49 | F | 0.0 | Fail | The minimum pass mark for any undergraduate course is 50. The cumulative grade point average is computed across all attempted courses, weighted by credit units, and is reported to two decimal places.
doc_title: Nakawa University Academic Handbook 2025/2026
citation: Nakawa University Academic Handbook 2025/2026, s. 6 (Grading Scheme), p. 4

text: A student who is graded F in a course must retake that course. A retake is taken the next time the course is offered and attracts a retake fee equal to the per-credit-unit tuition rate for the course. The mark recorded for a successful retake is capped at 50, that is, the minimum pass mark, regardless of the raw mark obtained. The capped mark replaces the failed mark in the computation of the cumulative grade point average, but the original attempt remains visible on the internal academic record. A student may retake a given course a maximum of three times. A student who fails the same course a fourth time is discontinued from the programme. A student must accumulate at least 45 credit units in an academic year to progress to the next year of study. A student who accumulates fewer than 45 credit units repeats the year.
doc_title: Nakawa University Academic Handbook 2025/2026
citation: Nakawa University Academic Handbook 2025/2026, s. 7 (Retakes and Progression), p. 4

text: A student may apply to defer study for a full semester or a full academic year. Deferment is not granted for part of a semester. The application is made on Form AR/11 not later than the end of the fourth week of the semester concerned, and is approved by the Academic Registrar. A deferring student pays a deferment maintenance fee of UGX 100,000 per semester deferred and retains their student number and programme place. The maximum cumulative deferment permitted over the course of an undergraduate programme is two semesters.
doc_title: Nakawa University Academic Handbook 2025/2026
citation: Nakawa University Academic Handbook 2025/2026, s. 8 (Deferment of Study), p. 5

text: Where a student's academic performance or ability to meet a deadline has been materially affected by circumstances beyond their control, the student may submit an Exceptional Circumstances application to the Faculty Board. The application must be submitted within ten working days of the circumstance arising, or within ten working days of the affected assessment, whichever is later. It must be accompanied by independent documentary evidence. Self-certification is not accepted for any application relating to a final examination.
doc_title: Nakawa University Academic Handbook 2025/2026
citation: Nakawa University Academic Handbook 2025/2026, s. 9 (Exceptional Circumstances), p. 5

text: It must be accompanied by independent documentary evidence. Self-certification is not accepted for any application relating to a final examination. The Faculty Board may, where the application is upheld, grant one of the following remedies: an extension of a submission deadline, a further attempt at an assessment as a first attempt, withdrawal from a course outside the normal deadline, or retrospective deferment. The Faculty Board does not have authority to alter a mark awarded by an examiner.
doc_title: Nakawa University Academic Handbook 2025/2026
citation: Nakawa University Academic Handbook 2025/2026, s. 9 (Exceptional Circumstances), p. 5

text: An undergraduate programme of three years must be completed within five years of first registration. An undergraduate programme of four years must be completed within six years of first registration. Periods of approved deferment are included in this count. A student who exceeds the maximum duration is discontinued.
doc_title: Nakawa University Academic Handbook 2025/2026
citation: Nakawa University Academic Handbook 2025/2026, s. 10 (Maximum Programme Duration), p. 5

text: The University is closed to teaching on gazetted public holidays of the Republic of Uganda. In addition, the University observes an administrative closure from 24 December 2025 to 2 January 2026 inclusive. Student Portal services remain available during the administrative closure, but the Academic Registry, Finance and Faculty offices are closed and no applications are processed.

text: These Regulations govern the conduct of all university examinations, including end of semester examinations, supplementary examinations, retake examinations and any timed assessment designated by Senate as an examination.
doc_title: Nakawa University Examination Regulations
citation: Nakawa University Examination Regulations, s. 1 (Application), p. 1

text: A student is eligible to sit an examination in a course only where all of the following are satisfied: The student is registered for the semester in which the examination falls. The student is registered for the specific course. The student has met the 75% attendance requirement for the course. The student has cleared at least sixty per cent (60%) of the semester tuition and has no outstanding balance from any previous semester. The student holds a valid Examination Permit generated from the Student Portal. A student who is not eligible and who nonetheless sits an examination has that examination result nullified.
doc_title: Nakawa University Examination Regulations
citation: Nakawa University Examination Regulations, s. 2 (Eligibility to Sit an Examination), p. 1

text: The Examination Permit is generated by the student from the Student Portal from the beginning of revision week. The Permit is printed on plain paper and carries a QR code that is verified by the invigilator. A student who arrives at an examination without a Permit is allowed to sit the paper provisionally, and must present the Permit to the Faculty Registrar within twenty-four hours. Where the Permit is not presented within twenty-four hours, the script is withheld and is released only after clearance. The Permit must be accompanied by the student's University Identity Card. A student with neither a Permit nor an Identity Card is not admitted to the examination room.
doc_title: Nakawa University Examination Regulations
citation: Nakawa University Examination Regulations, s. 3 (The Examination Permit), p. 2

text: Candidates are admitted to the examination room fifteen minutes before the start of the paper. A candidate who arrives within thirty minutes of the start of the paper is admitted and is given no additional time. A candidate who arrives more than thirty minutes after the start of the paper is not admitted. No candidate may leave the examination room during the first thirty minutes or the last fifteen minutes of the paper. The following are prohibited in the examination room: mobile telephones, smart watches, programmable calculators unless expressly permitted on the question paper, any written or printed material unless the paper is designated open book, and communication of any kind between candidates.
doc_title: Nakawa University Examination Regulations
citation: Nakawa University Examination Regulations, s. 4 (Conduct in the Examination Room), p. 2

text: Examination misconduct includes possession of unauthorised material, copying from another candidate, permitting another candidate to copy, communicating with another candidate, impersonation, and refusal to surrender material when directed by an invigilator. An invigilator who suspects misconduct records the facts on Form EX/3, impounds the material, allows the candidate to complete the paper, and submits the report to the Academic Registrar within twenty-four hours. Allegations of misconduct are heard by the University Examinations Disciplinary Committee. The candidate is notified in writing at least seven days before the hearing, may be accompanied by one person, and may call witnesses. The penalties available to the Committee are:
doc_title: Nakawa University Examination Regulations
citation: Nakawa University Examination Regulations, s. 5 (Examination Misconduct), p. 3

text: The penalties available to the Committee are: A written warning recorded on the internal academic record. Nullification of the result in the course concerned, with a grade of F. Nullification of all results in the semester concerned. Suspension for a stated period of one or two academic years. Expulsion from the University. Impersonation, whether by the candidate or the impersonator, carries a minimum penalty of expulsion where the allegation is proved.
doc_title: Nakawa University Examination Regulations
citation: Nakawa University Examination Regulations, s. 5 (Examination Misconduct), p. 3

text: A student who misses an examination without approved cause is graded F in that course and must retake it. A student who misses an examination with cause must submit a Missed Examination application on Form EX/9 within five working days of the date of the paper, with independent documentary evidence. Accepted causes are documented illness, bereavement of an immediate family member, and circumstances certified by the Dean as beyond the student's control. Where the application is upheld, the student sits the paper at the next available sitting, which is the retake and supplementary examination period in June. The attempt is recorded as a first attempt and the mark is not capped.
doc_title: Nakawa University Examination Regulations
citation: Nakawa University Examination Regulations, s. 6 (Missed Examinations), p. 4

text: Provisional results are published on the Student Portal on the dates set out in the Academic Calendar. Results are provisional until confirmed by Senate. A result withheld for non-payment of fees is displayed as WH on the Student Portal. A result withheld pending a disciplinary hearing is displayed as UR.
doc_title: Nakawa University Examination Regulations
citation: Nakawa University Examination Regulations, s. 7 (Release of Results), p. 4

text: A student who believes a mark is incorrect may apply for a remark within fourteen days of the publication of provisional results. The application is made on Form EX/12 and attracts a fee of UGX 30,000 per course, which is refunded where the mark changes. A remark is a full second marking by an independent examiner. The mark resulting from the remark stands, whether it is higher than, equal to, or lower than the original mark. A student is advised that a remark may reduce a mark. There is no further academic appeal on the substance of a mark. An appeal on procedural grounds is made under the Complaints, Appeals and Grievance Procedure.
doc_title: Nakawa University Examination Regulations
citation: Nakawa University Examination Regulations, s. 8 (Remarking and Appeals), p. 4

text: This Policy governs the assessment, payment and recovery of tuition and functional fees for all students of Nakawa University. It does not govern scholarships administered by external sponsors, which are governed by the agreement between the University and the sponsor.
doc_title: Nakawa University Student Fees and Financial Policy
citation: Nakawa University Student Fees and Financial Policy, s. 1 (Scope), p. 1

text: A student is liable for two categories of charge in each semester: Tuition, assessed per credit unit at the rate published for the programme and year of entry. The rate applicable to a student is the rate in force at the student's first registration and is not varied during the normal programme duration. Functional fees, being a fixed amount per semester covering registration, examination, identity card, library, laboratory and medical services. Functional fees for 2025/2026 are UGX 480,000 per semester for all undergraduate programmes.
doc_title: Nakawa University Student Fees and Financial Policy
citation: Nakawa University Student Fees and Financial Policy, s. 2 (Structure of Fees), p. 1

text: Fees are payable by bank deposit or mobile money to the University collection accounts published on the Student Portal. Cash is not received at any University office. A student may pay in two instalments in each semester: A first instalment of not less than sixty per cent (60%) of the total semester liability, due on the date published in the Academic Calendar. This instalment must clear before the student can complete registration. The balance of forty per cent (40%), due on the balance date published in the Academic Calendar. A payment is recognised when it is reflected on the student's Portal account. A student who has deposited funds that are not reflected within three working days presents the deposit slip to the Finance Help Desk with their student number.
doc_title: Nakawa University Student Fees and Financial Policy
citation: Nakawa University Student Fees and Financial Policy, s. 3 (Payment and Instalments), p. 2

text: A student who has not cleared the first instalment by the registration deadline is not registered for the semester. A student who has not cleared the balance by the balance date has examination results for that semester withheld and displayed as WH on the Student Portal. Withheld results are released within three working days of the account being cleared. An outstanding balance from a previous semester bars registration in any subsequent semester and bars participation in graduation.
doc_title: Nakawa University Student Fees and Financial Policy
citation: Nakawa University Student Fees and Financial Policy, s. 4 (Consequences of Non-Payment), p. 2

text: A student who formally drops a course within the add/drop period has the tuition for that course credited in full to their Portal account. A student who withdraws from a course after the add/drop deadline, whether or not the withdrawal is approved, is not entitled to a refund or credit of tuition for that course. A student who defers a semester under the Academic Handbook has tuition already paid for that semester carried forward to the semester of return. Functional fees are not carried forward and are not refunded. A student who is discontinued or who leaves the University is refunded any credit balance on application, less the functional fees for the semester in progress. Applications for refund are made on Form FIN/4 and are paid within thirty working days.
doc_title: Nakawa University Student Fees and Financial Policy
citation: Nakawa University Student Fees and Financial Policy, s. 5 (Refunds), p. 3

text: A late payment surcharge of two per cent (2%) of the outstanding amount is applied for each calendar month or part month by which a payment is late. The surcharge is applied automatically by the Portal and is itself part of the outstanding balance.
doc_title: Nakawa University Student Fees and Financial Policy
citation: Nakawa University Student Fees and Financial Policy, s. 6 (Late Payment), p. 3

text: A student who is unable to meet a published fees deadline may apply to the Bursar for a Revised Payment Plan. The application is made on Form FIN/9 before the deadline concerned and is supported by evidence of the circumstances. A Revised Payment Plan varies the dates on which amounts fall due. It does not reduce the total amount payable and it does not waive the late payment surcharge on amounts already overdue at the date of application. The Bursar decides an application within five working days. A student whose application is granted is treated as compliant with the deadline for the purposes of registration and examination eligibility, for as long as the Plan is honoured. A student who defaults on a Revised Payment Plan is immediately subject to Section 4.
doc_title: Nakawa University Student Fees and Financial Policy
citation: Nakawa University Student Fees and Financial Policy, s. 7 (Financial Hardship), p. 3

text: A student may generate a fees statement at any time from the Student Portal under Finance, then Statement of Account. The statement shows all assessments, payments, credits and surcharges for the current and all previous semesters. A stamped statement for presentation to a sponsor is obtained from the Finance Help Desk within two working days of request.
doc_title: Nakawa University Student Fees and Financial Policy
citation: Nakawa University Student Fees and Financial Policy, s. 8 (Fees Statements), p. 3

text: Every admitted student is issued two credentials: A Student Portal account, with the student number as the username. The Portal is used for registration, course selection, results, fees statements and the Examination Permit. A University email account in the form firstname.lastname@students.nakawa.ac.ug. This is the only address to which the University sends official communication. Accounts are created within five working days of the payment of the first instalment. The initial Portal password is the student's date of birth in the format DDMMYYYY and must be changed at first login.
doc_title: Nakawa University ICT and Student Portal Guidelines
citation: Nakawa University ICT and Student Portal Guidelines, s. 1 (University Accounts), p. 1

text: A student who has forgotten a Portal password uses the Forgot Password link on the Portal login page. A reset link is sent to the University email address and is valid for thirty minutes. A student who cannot access the University email account presents in person at the ICT Help Desk with a University Identity Card, or emails ithelp@nakawa.ac.ug from a previously registered alternative address. Password resets are not performed over the telephone and are not performed on the basis of a request from a third party.
doc_title: Nakawa University ICT and Student Portal Guidelines
citation: Nakawa University ICT and Student Portal Guidelines, s. 2 (Password Reset), p. 1

text: The Student Portal is available twenty-four hours a day except during scheduled maintenance, which takes place on the first Sunday of each month between 02:00 and 06:00 East Africa Time. Maintenance is not scheduled during a registration period, an add/drop period or an examination period. Where emergency maintenance is unavoidable during those periods, the Directorate publishes a notice on the Portal login page and extends any affected deadline by the duration of the outage.
doc_title: Nakawa University ICT and Student Portal Guidelines
citation: Nakawa University ICT and Student Portal Guidelines, s. 3 (Portal Availability and Maintenance), p. 2

text: Course not appearing in the selection list. The course is not offered to the student's programme and year, or the student has not been cleared by Finance. The student contacts the Head of Department in the first case and the Finance Help Desk in the second. Registration button disabled. The first instalment has not been recognised, or the biometric confirmation step has not been completed. The student checks the fees statement first, then attends the Faculty Registrar for biometrics. Examination Permit will not generate. The Permit generates only where the student is registered, has met attendance, and has no outstanding balance. The Portal displays the specific failing condition beneath the Generate button. Results not visible. Results marked WH are withheld for fees. Results marked UR are withheld pending a disciplinary matter. Results that are simply absent have not yet been submitted by the department.
doc_title: Nakawa University ICT and Student Portal Guidelines
citation: Nakawa University ICT and Student Portal Guidelines, s. 4 (Common Portal Problems), p. 2

text: University ICT facilities are provided for academic purposes. The following are prohibited and are disciplinary offences under the Student Regulations: Sharing account credentials with any other person. Accessing or attempting to access another person's account. Circumventing network controls, including the use of unauthorised proxies to bypass filtering. Using University facilities to store or distribute material that infringes copyright. Sending bulk unsolicited messages from a University account. The Directorate logs authentication events and network flows and retains those logs for one hundred and eighty days. Logs are disclosed to the Dean of Students only on a written request in connection with a disciplinary investigation.
doc_title: Nakawa University ICT and Student Portal Guidelines
citation: Nakawa University ICT and Student Portal Guidelines, s. 5 (Acceptable Use), p. 3

text: | Category | Items | Loan period | Renewals | |---|---|---|---| | Undergraduate | 4 | 14 days | 2 | | Postgraduate | 8 | 28 days | 3 | | Short Loan Collection | 1 | 3 hours, in-library | None | Renewal is performed on the Library catalogue or at the circulation desk, and is not permitted where another user has placed a hold on the item. text: The Library subscribes to electronic databases covering engineering, computing, business and health. Access from within the campus network is automatic. Access from outside the campus is through the EZproxy link on the Library website, authenticated with the University email address and the Portal password. Electronic resources are licensed for individual academic use. Systematic downloading of a database or of a complete journal issue breaches the licence, and the publisher suspends access for the entire University when it is detected.
doc_title: Nakawa University Library Services Guide
citation: Nakawa University Library Services Guide, s. 4 (Electronic Resources), p. 2

text: The Library provides silent study areas on the third floor, group discussion rooms on the second floor, and an open reading area on the ground floor. Group discussion rooms are booked through the Library catalogue, for a maximum of three hours per group per day, up to seven days in advance. A room not occupied within fifteen minutes of the booked start time is released. Reserving a seat by leaving belongings unattended is not permitted. Items left unattended for more than thirty minutes are removed to the lost property desk.
doc_title: Nakawa University Library Services Guide
citation: Nakawa University Library Services Guide, s. 5 (Study Spaces), p. 3

text: Past examination papers for the preceding five academic years are available in the Past Papers section of the Library website, organised by faculty, programme and course code. Marking schemes and model answers are not published and are not released on request.
doc_title: Nakawa University Library Services Guide
citation: Nakawa University Library Services Guide, s. 6 (Past Examination Papers), p. 3

text: Subject librarians hold consultation hours during teaching weeks and support literature searching, database selection and referencing. Consultations are booked on the Library website. The University's required citation style for undergraduate work is set by the Faculty. The Library provides guides for APA 7th edition, IEEE and Harvard styles, and supports Zotero and Mendeley.
doc_title: Nakawa University Library Services Guide
citation: Nakawa University Library Services Guide, s. 7 (Support for Research and Referencing), p. 3

text: Food is not permitted in the Library. Covered drinking containers are permitted except in the Special Collections room. Mobile telephones are set to silent throughout and calls are taken outside the building. Repeated breaches are reported to the Dean of Students under the Student Regulations.
doc_title: Nakawa University Library Services Guide
citation: Nakawa University Library Services Guide, s. 8 (Conduct in the Library), p. 3

text: This Code applies to every registered student of Nakawa University, on and off campus, where the conduct concerned affects the University, its members or its reputation. It applies from the date of first registration until the date of graduation or discontinuation. Conduct that is also a criminal offence may be dealt with under this Code whether or not criminal proceedings are brought.
doc_title: Nakawa University Student Regulations and Code of Conduct
publisher: Office of the Dean of Students
citation: Nakawa University Student Regulations and Code of Conduct, s. 1 (Application of the Code), p. 1

text: A student shall: Comply with the Academic Handbook, the Examination Regulations and all published University notices. Carry the University Identity Card while on campus and produce it on the request of an identified member of staff. Treat every member of the University community with respect, without regard to sex, ethnicity, religion, disability or nationality. Use University property and facilities with care.
doc_title: Nakawa University Student Regulations and Code of Conduct
publisher: Office of the Dean of Students
citation: Nakawa University Student Regulations and Code of Conduct, s. 2 (General Obligations), p. 1

text: Academic misconduct is the presentation of work for assessment that is not the student's own, or that misrepresents its sources. It includes: Plagiarism, being the use of another person's words, ideas, code or data without acknowledgement. Collusion, being unauthorised collaboration on work that is required to be individual. Fabrication, being the invention of data, results, sources or citations. Contract cheating, being the commissioning of work from another person or service, whether paid or unpaid. Unauthorised use of generative artificial intelligence, being the submission of AI-generated content as the student's own work where the assessment brief does not permit it. Coursework is screened by similarity detection software.
doc_title: Nakawa University Student Regulations and Code of Conduct
publisher: Office of the Dean of Students
citation: Nakawa University Student Regulations and Code of Conduct, s. 3 (Academic Integrity), p. 2

text: Coursework is screened by similarity detection software. A similarity score is not by itself a finding of misconduct; the decision rests with the Faculty Academic Integrity Officer, who considers the nature of the matched material. First instances of plagiarism in a coursework item are normally dealt with by the Faculty Academic Integrity Officer, who may require resubmission with the mark capped at the pass mark. Repeat instances, and all instances of contract cheating or fabrication, are referred to the Students Disciplinary Committee.
doc_title: Nakawa University Student Regulations and Code of Conduct
publisher: Office of the Dean of Students
citation: Nakawa University Student Regulations and Code of Conduct, s. 3 (Academic Integrity), p. 2

text: The following are non-academic offences under this Code: Violence, threats of violence, and physical or verbal intimidation. Sexual harassment, being unwanted conduct of a sexual nature that violates a person's dignity. Bullying and harassment, including by electronic means. Theft, wilful damage to property, and unauthorised entry to University premises. Possession or use of illegal drugs, and being on campus under the influence of alcohol in a manner that disrupts University activity. Disruption of teaching, examinations, administration or lawfully organised University events. Falsification of any University document, including identity cards, medical certificates, transcripts and fees receipts.
doc_title: Nakawa University Student Regulations and Code of Conduct
publisher: Office of the Dean of Students
citation: Nakawa University Student Regulations and Code of Conduct, s. 4 (Non-Academic Misconduct), p. 3

text: A complaint is made in writing to the Dean of Students. The Dean assesses the complaint within five working days and either dismisses it, resolves it informally with the consent of both parties, or refers it to the Students Disciplinary Committee. A student referred to the Committee is served with a written statement of the allegation and the evidence at least seven days before the hearing. The student may respond in writing, may attend the hearing, may be accompanied by one member of the University community, and may call witnesses. The Committee decides on the balance of probabilities. Its decision and reasons are given in writing within ten working days of the hearing.
doc_title: Nakawa University Student Regulations and Code of Conduct
publisher: Office of the Dean of Students
citation: Nakawa University Student Regulations and Code of Conduct, s. 5 (Disciplinary Procedure), p. 3

text: The penalties available to the Students Disciplinary Committee are: A written warning, held on the internal record for the remainder of the programme. A requirement to make good any loss or damage. Withdrawal of a specified privilege, including access to halls of residence or to specified facilities. Community service within the University, not exceeding forty hours. Suspension for a stated period. Expulsion. The Committee takes into account any previous finding of misconduct, the student's response, and any mitigating circumstances submitted.
doc_title: Nakawa University Student Regulations and Code of Conduct
publisher: Office of the Dean of Students
citation: Nakawa University Student Regulations and Code of Conduct, s. 6 (Penalties), p. 4

text: Where the Vice Chancellor is satisfied that a student's continued presence presents a risk to the safety of others or to the integrity of an investigation, the student may be suspended on an interim basis pending the hearing. Interim suspension is not a penalty and is not a finding of misconduct. It is reviewed every twenty-one days and lapses when the matter is concluded.
doc_title: Nakawa University Student Regulations and Code of Conduct
publisher: Office of the Dean of Students
citation: Nakawa University Student Regulations and Code of Conduct, s. 7 (Interim Suspension), p. 4

text: A student may appeal a decision of the Students Disciplinary Committee to the University Appeals Board within fourteen days of receiving the written decision. The grounds of appeal are limited to procedural irregularity, the availability of new evidence that could not reasonably have been presented earlier, and disproportionality of the penalty. An appeal is not a rehearing of the facts. The decision of the University Appeals Board is final within the University.
doc_title: Nakawa University Student Regulations and Code of Conduct
publisher: Office of the Dean of Students
citation: Nakawa University Student Regulations and Code of Conduct, s. 8 (Appeals), p. 4

text: The BSc Software Engineering is a four-year, full-time undergraduate programme of the Department of Computer Science in the Faculty of Engineering. The programme is accredited by the National Council for Higher Education. The programme requires 480 credit units in total, distributed as 120 credit units per year of study. A full-time student takes between 15 and 24 credit units per semester, subject to the load limits in the Academic Handbook.
doc_title: Course Handbook: BSc Software Engineering
publisher: Department of Computer Science, Faculty of Engineering
citation: Course Handbook: BSc Software Engineering, s. 1 (Programme Overview), p. 1

doc_title: Course Handbook: BSc Software Engineering
publisher: Department of Computer Science, Faculty of Engineering

text: Coursework in this programme consists of continuous assessment tests, practical assignments and group projects. Where a course has a group component, the group mark is moderated by an individual contribution factor derived from the version control history and the peer assessment return. A student who does not submit a peer assessment return by the published date receives an individual contribution factor of 1.0 and forfeits the right to query the moderation. The pass mark for every course is 50, as set by the Academic Handbook. There is no compensation between the coursework and examination components: a student who scores below 40 in the examination component is graded F for the course irrespective of the coursework mark.
doc_title: Course Handbook: BSc Software Engineering
publisher: Department of Computer Science, Faculty of Engineering
section_title: Assessment Rules Specific to the Programme
citation: Course Handbook: BSc Software Engineering, s. 4 (Assessment Rules Specific to the Programme), p. 2

text: Coursework is submitted through the Learning Management System by the time and date stated in the assessment brief. A submission that is late by up to twenty-four hours is marked and the mark is then reduced by ten percentage points. A submission that is late by more than twenty-four hours and up to seventy-two hours is capped at the pass mark of 50. A submission that is late by more than seventy-two hours is not marked and is graded zero. These deductions are not applied where an Exceptional Circumstances application under the Academic Handbook has been upheld. Technical failure of a student's personal equipment or personal internet connection is not accepted as grounds for an extension. Students are advised to submit a draft version well before the deadline, as the Learning Management System retains all submissions and marks the most recent one.
doc_title: Course Handbook: BSc Software Engineering
publisher: Department of Computer Science, Faculty of Engineering
citation: Course Handbook: BSc Software Engineering, s. 5 (Late Submission of Coursework), p. 3

text: Every student undertakes eight weeks of supervised industrial training in the recess term following Year 3. The placement is sought by the student and approved in advance by the Industrial Training Coordinator. Assessment consists of the host supervisor's confidential report, a written training report of not more than five thousand words, and an oral presentation held in the second week of Semester I of Year 4. Industrial training carries 6 credit units and is graded pass or fail. A student who fails industrial training repeats the placement in the following recess term and may not proceed to the Capstone Project until it is passed.
doc_title: Course Handbook: BSc Software Engineering
publisher: Department of Computer Science, Faculty of Engineering
citation: Course Handbook: BSc Software Engineering, s. 6 (Industrial Training), p. 3

text: The Capstone Project runs across both semesters of Year 4 and carries 12 credit units. Students work in groups of four to six members on a problem approved by the Department. The assessment components are the project proposal, three progress demonstrations, the final software artefact and its repository, the group engineering report, and an individual viva voce. Individual accountability is assessed through the version control history, the issue tracker and the individual viva. A student whose individual contribution cannot be evidenced in the repository may be awarded an individual mark that differs materially from the group mark.
doc_title: Course Handbook: BSc Software Engineering
publisher: Department of Computer Science, Faculty of Engineering
citation: Course Handbook: BSc Software Engineering, s. 7 (Capstone Project), p. 4

text: Every student is assigned a Personal Academic Tutor on first registration and retains the same tutor for the duration of the programme where possible. The tutor meets the student at least once per semester, advises on course selection and progression, and is the first point of contact for academic difficulty. A student may request a change of tutor by writing to the Head of Department, and no reason need be given.
doc_title: Course Handbook: BSc Software Engineering
publisher: Department of Computer Science, Faculty of Engineering
citation: Course Handbook: BSc Software Engineering, s. 8 (Academic Advising), p. 4

text: The Office of the Dean of Students coordinates non-academic support for students: health, counselling, disability support, financial guidance, chaplaincy and student governance. Services described in this document are available to all registered students at no additional charge unless stated.
doc_title: Nakawa University Student Support and Welfare Services
publisher: Office of the Dean of Students
citation: Nakawa University Student Support and Welfare Services, s. 1 (Overview), p. 1

text: The University Clinic is located at Block H and is open Monday to Friday from 08:00 to 20:00 and on Saturday from 09:00 to 13:00. Outside these hours the Clinic operates an on-call nurse reachable through the Security Control Room. The Clinic provides general consultation, basic laboratory tests, dispensing of listed medicines, sexual and reproductive health services, and referral to partner hospitals. Registered students are covered by the University medical scheme funded from the functional fees, which covers services at the Clinic and referral consultation at partner facilities, but does not cover in-patient admission, surgery, dentistry or optical services.
doc_title: Nakawa University Student Support and Welfare Services
publisher: Office of the Dean of Students
citation: Nakawa University Student Support and Welfare Services, s. 2 (University Health Services), p. 1

text: Registered students are covered by the University medical scheme funded from the functional fees, which covers services at the Clinic and referral consultation at partner facilities, but does not cover in-patient admission, surgery, dentistry or optical services. A medical certificate for use in an Exceptional Circumstances or Missed Examination application is issued by the Clinic only where the student was examined at the time of the illness. The Clinic does not issue retrospective certificates on the basis of a later account by the student.
doc_title: Nakawa University Student Support and Welfare Services
publisher: Office of the Dean of Students
citation: Nakawa University Student Support and Welfare Services, s. 2 (University Health Services), p. 1

text: The Counselling Service provides confidential individual counselling, group sessions and workshops on stress, anxiety, bereavement, relationships and academic pressure. Appointments are booked through the Portal under Student Services, then Counselling, or by attending the Counselling Office at Block H Room 4. Standard appointments are offered within five working days. A student in distress who attends without an appointment is seen the same day by the duty counsellor. Counselling records are held separately from academic records and are not disclosed to academic staff, to parents or to sponsors. Disclosure is made without consent only where there is a serious risk to the life of the student or of another person, and then only to the extent necessary. A student may ask the Counselling Service to provide supporting documentation for an Exceptional Circumstances application. The documentation confirms the existence and period of the circumstance and does not disclose its content.
doc_title: Nakawa University Student Support and Welfare Services
publisher: Office of the Dean of Students
citation: Nakawa University Student Support and Welfare Services, s. 3 (Counselling Service), p. 2

text: A student with a disability, long-term medical condition or specific learning difficulty registers with the Inclusive Learning Office at Block H Room 9, with supporting evidence. The Office prepares a Learning Support Agreement that records the adjustments to be made. Adjustments may include additional time in examinations, a separate examination room, materials in alternative formats, a note-taker, permission to record lectures, and adjusted deadlines for coursework. The Agreement is communicated to the Faculty and to the Examinations Office. Examination adjustments must be in place at least four weeks before the start of the examination period; an Agreement finalised later than that is applied from the following examination period.
doc_title: Nakawa University Student Support and Welfare Services
publisher: Office of the Dean of Students
citation: Nakawa University Student Support and Welfare Services, s. 4 (Disability and Inclusive Learning Support), p. 2

text: A student who is pregnant, or who is the primary carer of a child or of a dependent adult, may register the circumstance with the Dean of Students. The University provides a parenting room at Block H, flexibility in the scheduling of continuous assessment tests where the schedule conflicts with a documented care obligation, and access to deferment under the Academic Handbook where continued study is not practicable. Pregnancy is not grounds for discontinuation and a student may not be required to leave the programme on account of pregnancy.
doc_title: Nakawa University Student Support and Welfare Services
publisher: Office of the Dean of Students
citation: Nakawa University Student Support and Welfare Services, s. 5 (Students with Caring Responsibilities), p. 3

text: The Students Welfare Fund provides small, non-repayable emergency grants for immediate needs such as food, transport, medical costs and the replacement of essential materials lost in a fire or theft. Applications are made on Form DS/6 to the Dean of Students and are decided within three working days. The maximum grant is UGX 300,000 in an academic year. The Fund does not pay tuition or functional fees and is not a route to a fees waiver; a student with difficulty in meeting fees deadlines applies to the Bursar for a Revised Payment Plan under the Fees and Financial Policy.
doc_title: Nakawa University Student Support and Welfare Services
publisher: Office of the Dean of Students
citation: Nakawa University Student Support and Welfare Services, s. 6 (Financial Guidance and Emergency Assistance), p. 3

text: The Nakawa University Students Association represents students. Guild elections are held in the fourth week of Semester I. Every registered student is a member and is entitled to vote. Each Faculty elects student representatives to the Faculty Board, and the Association nominates student members to the Senate committees on which student representation is provided for.
doc_title: Nakawa University Student Support and Welfare Services
publisher: Office of the Dean of Students
citation: Nakawa University Student Support and Welfare Services, s. 7 (Student Governance), p. 3

text: A concern about harassment, sexual misconduct or safeguarding is reported to the Dean of Students in person, or through the confidential reporting form on the Portal under Student Services, then Report a Concern. A report may be made anonymously. An anonymous report is recorded and informs the University's response, but the University's ability to take disciplinary action on an anonymous report is limited because the alleged party must be told the case against them. A student who makes a report in good faith is protected from any detriment arising from having made it.
doc_title: Nakawa University Student Support and Welfare Services
publisher: Office of the Dean of Students
section_title: Reporting a Safeguarding or Harassment Concern
citation: Nakawa University Student Support and Welfare Services, s. 8 (Reporting a Safeguarding or Harassment Concern), p. 3

text: A student is eligible to graduate where all of the following are satisfied: The student has passed every course required by the programme and accumulated the total credit units required. The student has completed the programme within the maximum duration permitted by the Academic Handbook. The student has no outstanding tuition, functional fees, library charges or other University debt. The student has returned all University property and obtained clearance. The results have been confirmed by Senate. A student who meets the academic requirements but has not obtained clearance is not presented for graduation and is deferred to the next ceremony.
doc_title: Nakawa University Graduation and Academic Awards Policy
citation: Nakawa University Graduation and Academic Awards Policy, s. 1 (Eligibility to Graduate), p. 1

text: The class of an undergraduate award is determined by the cumulative grade point average computed over all courses counting toward the award. | Cumulative GPA | Class of award | |---|---| | 4.40 - 5.00 | First Class Honours | | 3.60 - 4.39 | Second Class Honours, Upper Division | | 2.80 - 3.59 | Second Class Honours, Lower Division | | 2.00 - 2.79 | Pass | The cumulative grade point average is not rounded for the purposes of classification. A student with a cumulative grade point average of 4.39 is classified in the Upper Division and not in the First Class. A student who has been found guilty of examination misconduct resulting in the nullification of a semester's results is not eligible for First Class Honours.
doc_title: Nakawa University Graduation and Academic Awards Policy
citation: Nakawa University Graduation and Academic Awards Policy, s. 2 (Classification of Awards), p. 2

text: Clearance is completed on the Portal under Graduation, then Clearance. The Portal collects confirmation from the Library, the Directorate of Finance, the Halls of Residence, the relevant Department and the Directorate of ICT Services. Each unit confirms or raises an objection within five working days. An objection states the outstanding matter and the action required to resolve it. Clearance opens when the provisional graduation list is published and closes fourteen days before the ceremony.
doc_title: Nakawa University Graduation and Academic Awards Policy
citation: Nakawa University Graduation and Academic Awards Policy, s. 3 (Clearance), p. 2

text: The provisional graduation list is published on the Portal on the date in the Academic Calendar. A student who expects to be on the list and is not, or whose name, programme or class is stated incorrectly, submits a query to the Academic Registrar before the published query deadline. A query submitted after the deadline is considered for the following ceremony. Names are printed on certificates exactly as they appear on the admission record, and a change of name is effected only on presentation of a statutory instrument or other legal document before the query deadline.
doc_title: Nakawa University Graduation and Academic Awards Policy
citation: Nakawa University Graduation and Academic Awards Policy, s. 4 (The Provisional Graduation List), p. 3

text: Graduands attend the ceremony in academic dress appropriate to the award. Academic dress is hired from the University at a charge published with the graduation notice, and is returned within three working days of the ceremony. A graduand who does not wish to attend the ceremony indicates this on the Portal and graduates in absentia. Certificates for graduands in absentia are collected from the Academic Registry from ten working days after the ceremony, in person and on production of the University Identity Card, or by a representative holding a letter of authority and a copy of the graduand's identification.
doc_title: Nakawa University Graduation and Academic Awards Policy
citation: Nakawa University Graduation and Academic Awards Policy, s. 5 (The Ceremony), p. 3

text: Each graduand is issued one certificate and one official transcript without charge. A replacement certificate is issued only where the original is lost or destroyed, on a sworn declaration and payment of the published charge, and is marked as a replacement. Additional official transcripts are issued on request and on payment of the published charge, within five working days. A verification of award for an employer or a further education institution is provided by the Academic Registry on written request from the institution concerned, with the graduand's consent.
doc_title: Nakawa University Graduation and Academic Awards Policy
citation: Nakawa University Graduation and Academic Awards Policy, s. 6 (Certificates and Transcripts), p. 3

text: Senate may confer an award posthumously where a student had substantially completed the programme. Senate may confer an aegrotat award where a student is prevented by illness from completing the assessment and the available evidence indicates that the student would have passed. An aegrotat award is unclassified.
doc_title: Nakawa University Graduation and Academic Awards Policy
citation: Nakawa University Graduation and Academic Awards Policy, s. 7 (Posthumous and Aegrotat Awards), p. 3

text: The University maintains five halls of residence with a combined capacity of one thousand four hundred beds. Halls are single-sex in their sleeping accommodation and shared in their common facilities. A residence place is for one academic year and does not run through the recess term, except for students on approved recess-term academic activity, who apply separately.
doc_title: Nakawa University Accommodation and Halls of Residence Policy
citation: Nakawa University Accommodation and Halls of Residence Policy, s. 1 (Halls of Residence), p. 1

text: Applications for residence open on the Portal under Accommodation on the first working day of July and close on the last working day of July. Where applications exceed capacity, places are allocated in the following order of priority: Students with a disability or medical condition requiring accommodation on campus, as evidenced by a Learning Support Agreement. First-year students whose home district is outside the Kampala metropolitan area. Finalist students. All other applicants, by ballot. The outcome is published on the Portal within fourteen days of the closing date. An offer not accepted and paid for within seven days lapses and the place passes to the next applicant on the list.
doc_title: Nakawa University Accommodation and Halls of Residence Policy
citation: Nakawa University Accommodation and Halls of Residence Policy, s. 2 (Allocation), p. 1

text: Residence charges are payable per semester, in advance, and are separate from tuition and functional fees. The charge for 2025/2026 is UGX 950,000 per semester for a shared room of four beds and UGX 1,400,000 per semester for a shared room of two beds. A resident who vacates before the end of a semester forfeits the charge for that semester. A resident whose place is withdrawn for disciplinary reasons forfeits the charge for that semester.
doc_title: Nakawa University Accommodation and Halls of Residence Policy
citation: Nakawa University Accommodation and Halls of Residence Policy, s. 3 (Residence Charges), p. 2

text: Every resident signs a Residence Agreement. The Agreement requires the resident to: Occupy only the allocated bed space and not to transfer or sublet it. Admit visitors only between 08:00 and 22:00, and to sign visitors in at the Hall desk. Overnight visitors are not permitted. Refrain from cooking in rooms. Cooking is permitted only in the Hall kitchens. Refrain from keeping electrical heating appliances, candles and other naked flames in rooms. Keep the room in a clean and safe condition and allow inspection on reasonable notice. Vacate the Hall within forty-eight hours of the end of the examination period. Breach of the Residence Agreement is dealt with by the Warden and may be referred to the Dean of Students under the Student Regulations.
doc_title: Nakawa University Accommodation and Halls of Residence Policy
citation: Nakawa University Accommodation and Halls of Residence Policy, s. 4 (Conditions of Residence), p. 2

text: A maintenance request is logged on the Portal under Accommodation, then Report a Fault, or at the Hall desk. | Category | Examples | Target response | |---|---|---| | Emergency | Burst pipe, electrical hazard, failed external door lock | 4 hours | | Urgent | No water, no power to a room, blocked toilet | 24 hours | | Routine | Faulty socket, broken furniture, dripping tap | 5 working days | A resident is charged for damage that is not fair wear and tear. Where responsibility cannot be attributed to an individual, the cost of damage to a shared area is shared among the residents of that area.
doc_title: Nakawa University Accommodation and Halls of Residence Policy
citation: Nakawa University Accommodation and Halls of Residence Policy, s. 5 (Maintenance and Repairs), p. 3

text: Halls are staffed at the entrance at all hours. Residents present the University Identity Card on entry. Rooms are fitted with individual locks. The University does not insure residents' personal property, and residents are advised to insure valuable items independently. Lost keys are reported immediately and are replaced at a charge of UGX 40,000.
doc_title: Nakawa University Accommodation and Halls of Residence Policy
citation: Nakawa University Accommodation and Halls of Residence Policy, s. 6 (Security), p. 3

text: A residence place is withdrawn where a student ceases to be registered, is suspended or expelled, defaults on residence charges for more than thirty days, or commits a serious breach of the Residence Agreement. A student whose place is withdrawn for default may be readmitted to residence in a later semester on clearing the debt, subject to availability.
doc_title: Nakawa University Accommodation and Halls of Residence Policy
citation: Nakawa University Accommodation and Halls of Residence Policy, s. 7 (Withdrawal of a Residence Place), p. 3

text: The University does not inspect, approve or endorse private accommodation, and is not a party to any agreement between a student and a private landlord. The Dean of Students maintains a noticeboard of properties offered by landlords and a guidance note on matters to check before signing a tenancy. Students are advised not to pay any deposit before viewing a property and obtaining a written agreement.
doc_title: Nakawa University Accommodation and Halls of Residence Policy
citation: Nakawa University Accommodation and Halls of Residence Policy, s. 8 (Private Accommodation), p. 3

text: This Procedure applies to a complaint by a student about a service, a decision or the conduct of a member of the University, and to an appeal against an academic decision on procedural grounds. This Procedure does not apply to: The academic judgement of an examiner on the merits of a piece of work. A disagreement with a mark is dealt with by remarking under the Examination Regulations. A disciplinary decision of the Students Disciplinary Committee, which is appealed to the University Appeals Board under the Student Regulations. A complaint about admission, which is dealt with under the Admissions Policy.
doc_title: Nakawa University Complaints, Appeals and Grievance Procedure
citation: Nakawa University Complaints, Appeals and Grievance Procedure, s. 1 (Scope), p. 1

text: A student who raises a complaint in good faith suffers no disadvantage as a result. A complaint is considered by a person who was not involved in the matter complained of. A student is informed of the outcome and the reasons for it in writing.
doc_title: Nakawa University Complaints, Appeals and Grievance Procedure
citation: Nakawa University Complaints, Appeals and Grievance Procedure, s. 2 (Principles), p. 1

text: A student raises the matter with the person or office concerned, or with the Head of Department, within twenty working days of the event. The matter is considered and the student receives a response within ten working days. Most complaints are resolved at this stage and no written record is kept beyond the response. A student who is not satisfied, or for whom informal resolution is not appropriate because of the seriousness of the matter, proceeds to Stage Two.
doc_title: Nakawa University Complaints, Appeals and Grievance Procedure
citation: Nakawa University Complaints, Appeals and Grievance Procedure, s. 3 (Stage One: Informal Resolution), p. 2

text: A formal complaint is submitted on Form AR/20 to the Academic Registrar within ten working days of the Stage One response, or within twenty working days of the event where Stage One was not appropriate. The complaint states the facts, what has already been done to resolve it, and the outcome sought. Supporting evidence is attached. The Academic Registrar appoints an investigating officer who was not involved in the matter. The investigating officer may interview the student and any other person, and requests documents from any office of the University. The outcome is communicated in writing within twenty-five working days of receipt, with the findings, the reasons and any remedy. Where the investigation cannot be completed within that period, the student is informed of the reason and given a revised date.
doc_title: Nakawa University Complaints, Appeals and Grievance Procedure
citation: Nakawa University Complaints, Appeals and Grievance Procedure, s. 4 (Stage Two: Formal Complaint), p. 2

text: A student who is dissatisfied with the Stage Two outcome may request a review by the Vice Chancellor within fourteen days of the outcome. A review is not a re-investigation. The grounds for review are limited to: The procedure was not followed and this affected the outcome. The outcome was not reasonable on the evidence considered. New material evidence is available that was not reasonably available at Stage Two. The Vice Chancellor issues a Completion of Procedures letter within twenty working days, which concludes the University's internal procedure.
doc_title: Nakawa University Complaints, Appeals and Grievance Procedure
citation: Nakawa University Complaints, Appeals and Grievance Procedure, s. 5 (Stage Three: Review), p. 3

text: An appeal against a decision of a Faculty Board or of Senate concerning progression, discontinuation or classification is submitted to the Academic Registrar within fourteen days of the decision being communicated. The grounds are limited to procedural irregularity, the existence of exceptional circumstances that were not considered for good reason, and bias or prejudice in the decision-making process. A disagreement with academic judgement is not a ground of appeal. An appeal is heard by the Academic Appeals Committee, which may uphold the decision, refer the matter back to the original decision-maker for reconsideration, or substitute its own decision.
doc_title: Nakawa University Complaints, Appeals and Grievance Procedure
citation: Nakawa University Complaints, Appeals and Grievance Procedure, s. 6 (Academic Appeals on Procedural Grounds), p. 3

text: An anonymous complaint is recorded and may inform a wider review, but is not normally investigated under this Procedure because the student cannot be given an outcome and the other party cannot be given the case against them. A complaint made by a parent, sponsor or other third party is not considered unless the student confirms in writing that the third party acts on their behalf.
doc_title: Nakawa University Complaints, Appeals and Grievance Procedure
citation: Nakawa University Complaints, Appeals and Grievance Procedure, s. 7 (Anonymous and Third-Party Complaints), p. 3

text: Records of formal complaints are held by the Academic Registrar for six years and are held separately from the student's academic record. A complaint has no effect on assessment. The Academic Registrar reports annually to Senate on the number, type and outcome of formal complaints, and on any changes to University practice made as a result.
doc_title: Nakawa University Complaints, Appeals and Grievance Procedure
citation: Nakawa University Complaints, Appeals and Grievance Procedure, s. 8 (Records and Monitoring), p. 3
